channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: NHS cannot afford the beds it needs this winter, admits NHSE
item.description: The NHS “potentially” lacks the beds to deal with increased emergency care demand over the winter because of cost constraints, NHS England has admitted to MPs.

item.title: Consultants strike ‘paused’
item.description: Strikes planned by medical consultants for later this month have been “paused”, with their union saying government has agreed to open negotiations.

item.title: ICBs take action against top wheelchair provider
item.description: Several integrated care boards have taken formal action against the NHS’s biggest independent wheelchair provider, whose long delays and poor communication have now been criticised by an ombudsman.

item.title: CQC still ‘adversarial and fault-finding’, NHS bosses warn
item.description: NHS bosses have warned of a “punitive” inspection culture at the CQC, two years into the regulator’s recovery from a damning review.

item.title: Terror attack funding doesn’t meet trusts’ ask
item.description: NHS England has outlined spending worth about £34m to make ambulance services better able to respond to terror attacks – but the settlement appears to fall well short of ambulance trusts’ asks.

item.title: Biggest bailout in five years given to ailing trust
item.description: A teaching trust received £125m in emergency cash support last year – the largest payment of its kind so far – it has emerged.

item.title: NHSE blocking redundant staff from being rehired
item.description: NHS England has blocked staff who have been made redundant from returning to work at the organisation – a move employees say is “moving the goalposts” on their departure terms.

item.title: Fraudster secretly held DHSC and trust jobs
item.description: A civil servant who secretly held eight public sector jobs on full-time salaries, including roles at an NHS trust, the Department of Health and Social Care and the UK Health Security Agency, has been convicted of fraud.

item.title: Suspension of subco ‘costing trust £30m’
item.description: A trust says it now faces a £30m financial gap after plans to outsource more workers to its wholly owned subsidiary company were put on hold pending national guidance from NHS England.

item.title: System’s 10 maternity units ‘all losing money’
item.description: Some of South London’s maternity units have “unsustainably low” birth numbers and may need to close, alongside centralisation of children’s services and surgery, a review has found.

item.title: Revealed: The tech firms set to replace Palantir
item.description: A British technology company is being lined up to replace Palantir as lead supplier of the federated data platform from 2029, with the US firm’s existing contract likely to be extended until then.

item.title: Child death files deleted ‘methodically and selectively’
item.description: Records of child, neonatal, and maternal deaths held by a trust’s medical examiner service were “methodically and selectively” deleted, an external investigation has found.

item.title: 1,000 staff set for compulsory redundancy
item.description: A total of 1,000 jobs are set to go at commissioning support units after ministers approved a long-delayed case for redundancy, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Trust faces ‘unpalatable’ cuts or potential leadership changes
item.description: A trust has said it must consider “unpalatable” options to achieve its financial plan this year after it was warned that a failure to break even would trigger a “formal leadership review”.

item.title: ‘Temporary’ quango has no end date, staff told
item.description: The government has no plan for when or how it will shut down the new quango that will employ thousands of NHS England regional teams, staff have been told – a day after ministers stressed the organisation would be “temporary”.

item.title: Managers’ pay rise blocked at 28 trusts, but ICBs spared
item.description: Very senior managers at 28 struggling trusts will not receive this year’s 3 per cent pay rise, ministers have confirmed.

item.title: ‘Shocking’ rise in maternal readmissions revealed
item.description: The rate of women readmitted to hospital within six weeks of giving birth has risen by more than a third in less than three years, HSJ analysis of unpublished data suggests.

item.title: NHSE warns ICBs over staffing and capability gaps
item.description: NHS England criticised staffing and capacity issues at several integrated care boards, a year after instructing them to cut their staffing by half.

item.title: Victims demand tougher restrictions on snooping
item.description: Victims of the Southport and Nottingham attacks have told ministers and NHS leaders that far stricter, more robust processes are needed to stop staff snooping on patient records – and that actions outlined so far are not enough.

item.title: Vulnerable patients’ long dental waits ‘buried’
item.description: NHS England has been accused of continuing to “bury” evidence of the very long waits for dental treatment endured by people with complex needs, the British Dental Association has said.
